topic: EPA general permit: who is covered
rule: 40 CFR 229.1(a) grants a general permit (no application) to (1) anyone subject to MPRSA Title I to transport human remains from the United States for burial at sea, and (2) owners/operators of US-registered or US-flagged vessels or aircraft, and US government entities, to transport human remains from any location and bury them at sea.
quote: are hereby granted a general permit to transport human remains from any location for the purpose of burial at sea
appliesTo: Any vessel departing a US port carrying remains; any US-flagged vessel anywhere
notes: Text retrieved from the eCFR versioner API (www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-11-01/title-40.xml?part=229&section=229.1). Most large cruise ships are foreign-flagged, so the 'from any location' branch does not reach them; the 'from the United States' branch does when the ship departed a US port with the remains aboard.

rule: Cremated remains may be placed in or on ocean waters at any depth, but no closer than 3 nautical miles from land. 'Land' is measured from the territorial-sea baseline closest to the site (40 CFR 229.1(b)).
quote: Cremated remains shall be buried in or on ocean waters without regard to the depth limitations specified in paragraph (a)(2) of this section provided that such burial shall take place no closer than 3 nautical miles from land.
appliesTo: Burials under the EPA general permit
notes: The 600-foot depth rule in (a)(2) applies only to non-cremated (whole-body) burials. Because 'land' is the baseline, 3 nm is counted from the baseline, not from the visible beach, which can matter in bays.

rule: Flowers and wreaths may be placed at the burial site under the general permit only if made of materials readily decomposable in the marine environment.
quote: Flowers and wreaths consisting of materials which are readily decomposable in the marine environment may be disposed of
appliesTo: Burials under the EPA general permit
notes: The regulation text itself does not list banned items (plastic, metal, balloons). Statements that non-decomposable items need a separate permit come from EPA web guidance, which could not be opened (see US-06).

rule: Every burial under the general permit must be reported within 30 days to the EPA Regional Administrator of the Region from which the vessel carrying the remains departed.
quote: All burials conducted under this general permit shall be reported within 30 days to the Regional Administrator of the Region from which the vessel carrying the remains departed.
appliesTo: The person conducting the burial (in practice the family or the vessel operator)
notes: The regulation does not say who files; EPA guidance reportedly expects the person conducting the burial or the vessel operator. Not verified.

topic: EPA Burial at Sea Reporting Tool
rule: EPA's online Burial at Sea Reporting Tool (https://burialatsea.epa.gov/) takes the 30-day report, as a guest or with an account. It asks for contact details of the person responsible for the arrangements (a funeral director, a relative or a designated person) and of the person responsible for the vessel, the deceased's name, burial date and location (coordinates in decimal degrees if known, or picked on a map). No death certificate needs to be sent.
citation: EPA, Burial at Sea page; Burial at Sea Reporting Tool Fact Sheet (May 13, 2019)
quote: This individual may be a funeral director, a relative of the deceased, or a person designated to report the burial at sea.
notes: Fact sheet PDF and the EPA Burial at Sea page opened directly on 2026-11-21. The EPA page adds: 'Please note that you do not need to submit documentation, such as a Certificate of Death, to the EPA when reporting a burial at sea.' The tool host burialatsea.epa.gov itself is outside this session's network and was not opened; its address is confirmed by both EPA documents.

topic: EPA Burial at Sea web page and FAQ
rule: EPA's Burial at Sea page (last updated August 26, 2026) confirms: the MPRSA general permit at 40 CFR 229.1 covers cremated remains; no application, prior notice or fee; cremated remains in ocean waters of any depth at least three nautical miles from land; 'three nautical miles from shore' measured from the ordinary low water mark or a closing line across bays and rivers; pets and non-human remains excluded, and pet ashes may not be mixed with human ashes; only readily decomposable flowers and wreaths; ashes may be placed in a container that has no plastic, does not float and ideally degrades quickly; no balloons, rockets or burning boats; report within 30 days to the EPA Region the vessel departed from.
quote: Cremated remains shall be buried in or on ocean waters of any depth provided that such burial takes place at least three nautical miles from land.
notes: Opened directly on 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quote checked word for word. Page states 'Last updated on August 26, 2026'.

topic: MPRSA scope: what 'ocean waters' and 'dumping' mean
rule: EPA's ocean dumping regulations prohibit, without a permit: transporting any material from the United States to dump it in ocean waters; for US-registered or US-flagged vessels, transporting material from any location to dump it; and dumping material transported from outside the US into the US territorial sea or the contiguous zone to 12 nm where it may affect the territorial sea or US territory. 'Ocean waters' are the waters seaward of the baseline, including the territorial sea and contiguous zone.
quote: No person shall dump any material transported from a location outside the United States: (i) Into the territorial sea of the United States
appliesTo: US-flagged vessels anywhere; any vessel transporting material from the US; any vessel dumping in the US territorial sea
notes: Text from the eCFR API. These provisions implement MPRSA section 101 (33 U.S.C. 1411); the statute itself was not opened (uscode.house.gov blocked). Consequence: a foreign-flagged cruise ship that loaded the remains abroad and scatters them on the high seas outside 12 nm is outside MPRSA; the same ship departing Miami with the remains aboard is inside it.

topic: Inland waters and the Clean Water Act
rule: EPA: scattering in lakes, rivers or other inland waters is not subject to federal regulation under the MPRSA; states may regulate it, some states prohibit it, and states may authorize burials in inland waters (rivers, lakes, bays) under state law and/or the Clean Water Act. Families should contact the state environmental agency, health agency or mortuary board.
citation: Clean Water Act, 33 U.S.C. 1251 et seq.; EPA Burial at Sea page
quote: Scattering of cremated remains in lakes, rivers, or other inland waters is not subject to federal regulation under the MPRSA.
notes: Opened directly on 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quote checked word for word.

topic: Glacier Bay National Park and Preserve
rule: In any NPS area, scattering cremated human ashes is prohibited except under a permit or in designated areas on conditions set by the superintendent. Glacier Bay's waters are park waters, so this rule applies there; no Glacier Bay-specific ash-scattering page was found.
quote: The scattering of human ashes from cremation is prohibited, except pursuant to the terms and conditions of a permit, or in designated areas according to conditions which may be established by the superintendent.
appliesTo: Anyone in a National Park System unit, including cruise passengers in Glacier Bay
notes: The rule text is confirmed via eCFR. Whether 36 CFR 2.62 reaches waters of Glacier Bay depends on NPS jurisdiction over those waters (36 CFR 1.2); Glacier Bay's vessel rules (36 CFR part 13, subpart N) contain no provision on ashes (searched; none found). The park's compendium (home.nps.gov) could not be opened. A web search found no Glacier Bay ash page; it suggested contacting the park (907-697-2230). A cruise line's own policy cannot substitute for an NPS permit.

topic: NPS parks with ash-scattering permit pages
rule: Several NPS units publish special-use-permit pages for scattering cremated remains (e.g. Gulf Islands, Cape Lookout, Biscayne, Yellowstone), showing that the 36 CFR 2.62 permit route is used in practice, including in coastal and marine parks.
notes: URLs found by web search: home.nps.gov/guis/planyourvisit/scattering-remains-permits.htm, home.nps.gov/calo/planyourvisit/sup-cremains.htm, nps.gov/bisc/..., home.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/ashscattering.htm. Pages not read in full.

topic: National Marine Sanctuaries: Monterey Bay, cruise ships
rule: In Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary, discharging or depositing any material from a cruise ship is prohibited except clean engine/generator cooling water, exhaust, clean bilge water or anchor wash. Cremated remains are not on that exception list.
quote: Discharging or depositing from within or into the Sanctuary any material or other matter from a cruise ship except clean vessel engine cooling water
appliesTo: Cruise ships in Monterey Bay NMS
notes: Text from eCFR API (part 922, 2026-11-01). The prohibitions can be lifted by a sanctuary permit or authorization (see US-15), not by a cruise line's policy. Whether NOAA treats ash scattering as a 'discharge or deposit' in practice is not stated in the regulation; NOAA guidance could not be opened.

topic: National Marine Sanctuaries: Greater Farallones, cruise ships
rule: Greater Farallones NMS uses the same structure: discharges from vessels other than cruise ships have listed exceptions, and cruise-ship discharges are separately restricted. No exception for cremated remains appears.
quote: Discharging or depositing from within or into the Sanctuary, other than from a cruise ship, any material or other matter except
notes: Text from eCFR API; full cruise-ship subparagraph not quoted here.

rule: Channel Islands NMS prohibits discharging or depositing any material within or into the sanctuary except listed items (fishing bait, certain treated sewage, etc.). Cremated remains are not listed.
quote: Discharging or depositing from within or into the Sanctuary any material or other matter except
notes: Text from eCFR API.

topic: National Marine Sanctuaries: Florida Keys and Hawaiian Humpback
rule: Florida Keys NMS prohibits discharging or depositing any material from within the sanctuary except fishing bait, routine vessel water and cooling water/exhaust. Hawaiian Islands Humpback Whale NMS prohibits discharges only where the activity requires a federal or state permit and is conducted without it or out of compliance, so a burial complying with the EPA general permit appears not to breach it. A Florida Keys sanctuary page reportedly says ashes may be scattered only in federal sanctuary waters more than 3 nm from land, with a permit form.
quote: Requires a Federal or State permit, license, lease, or other authorization
notes: Regulation text confirmed via eCFR; the Hawaii reading is an inference from the text, not an agency statement. Florida Keys guidance (floridakeys.noaa.gov/permits/special-use.html) known only from a search summary; NOAA hosts were blocked.

rule: NOAA may issue special use permits only for activity categories it has noticed in the Federal Register. NOAA's permit materials reportedly list 'disposal of cremated human remains within or into' sanctuaries as a special-use-permit category; a 2013 Federal Register notice proposed dropping a 'commercial operator' limit so private individuals could qualify. Superintendents may also issue ONMS 'authorizations' of another agency's approval in certain sanctuaries.
quote: The Director will not issue a special use permit for any category of activity unless the Director has published a notice in the Federal Register
appliesTo: Operators and individuals scattering in sanctuaries
notes: 922.31/922.36 text confirmed via eCFR. The cremated-remains category and the 2013 proposal are known only from search summaries; the final outcome of the 2013 proposal was not found. sanctuaries.noaa.gov/management/permits/special.html could not be opened.

rule: No Hawaii Department of Health rule on ocean scattering was found. The only Hawaii rule read that names scattering of cremated remains (HAR 20-26-40) concerns University of Hawaii management areas on Mauna Kea, not the ocean.
quote: The scattering of cremated human remains is allowed within the UH management areas, consistent with this chapter and policies and procedures established by the president.
notes: LII copy opened 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quote checked; not relevant to sea scattering. A 2000 Star-Bulletin column says DLNR advised no Health Department permit is needed to scatter ashes at sea (secondary, dated). Federal EPA rules (US-01 to US-04) and the Humpback Whale sanctuary (US-14) still apply.

rule: No Alaska state rule on scattering ashes in state waters was found. Secondary sources (Nolo) say Alaska has no state law on where ashes may be scattered.
notes: dec.alaska.gov returned HTTP 403 on 2026-11-21. Federal EPA rules apply offshore (US-01 to US-04) and NPS rules in Glacier Bay (US-09). Cunard's policy of not lowering ashes in Alaska state waters is operator policy, not law.

rule: A coastal state's sovereignty extends over its territorial sea (Art. 2), whose breadth may be set up to 12 nautical miles from the baselines (Art. 3). In a contiguous zone of up to 24 nm the coastal state may exercise the control necessary to prevent and punish infringement of its customs, fiscal, immigration or sanitary laws within its territory or territorial sea (Art. 33). A ship inside a country's territorial sea is therefore within that state's sovereignty, including any rules it has on ashes.
quote: Every State has the right to establish the breadth of its territorial sea up to a limit not exceeding 12 nautical miles, measured from baselines determined in accordance with this Convention.
appliesTo: All ships in a coastal state's waters
notes: Opened directly on 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200, official UN PDF); Arts. 2, 3 and 33 read in full and quote checked word for word. The 12 nm figure is a maximum; some states claim less. UNCLOS says nothing specific about cremated remains; the application to ashes is a reading of the sovereignty rule, not treaty text.

rule: Ships sail under the flag of one state and, save in exceptional cases expressly provided for in treaties or UNCLOS, are subject to its exclusive jurisdiction on the high seas (Art. 92(1)). Beyond national waters, the flag state's law therefore governs what happens on board, including a scattering.
quote: Ships shall sail under the flag of one State only and, save in exceptional cases expressly provided for in international treaties or in this Convention, shall be subject to its exclusive jurisdiction on the high seas.
notes: Opened directly 2026-11-21; quote checked word for word. Which flag-state laws (Bahamas, Panama, Malta, Bermuda, Italy) address ashes was not researched here. Note that Art. 210(5) and Art. 216 also give the coastal state and the loading state roles for dumping, so flag-state jurisdiction is not the only rule that can apply.

rule: UNCLOS defines 'dumping' as any deliberate disposal of wastes or other matter from vessels at sea, but excludes 'placement of matter for a purpose other than the mere disposal thereof' if not contrary to the Convention's aims (Art. 1(1)(5)). States must ensure dumping is not carried out without permission of their competent authorities (Art. 210(3)), and dumping within the territorial sea, the EEZ or onto the continental shelf needs the express prior approval of the coastal state (Art. 210(5)). UNCLOS does not say whether scattering cremated remains is 'dumping'; national laws decide.
quote: Dumping within the territorial sea and the exclusive economic zone or onto the continental shelf shall not be carried out without the express prior approval of the coastal State
notes: Opened directly 2026-11-21; Art. 1(1)(5) and Art. 210 read in full, quote checked. Whether ash scattering is 'dumping' or 'placement for a purpose other than mere disposal' is not addressed in the text; states differ (the US treats burial of remains as dumping under a general permit; the UK, Australia and the Netherlands say no permit is needed for ashes; see their entries). Art. 216 (enforcement) not re-read this round.

rule: The IMO page confirms the London Convention 1972 and the 1996 Protocol regulate dumping of wastes and other matter at sea; under the Protocol 'all dumping is prohibited, except for possibly acceptable wastes on the so-called reverse list'. The IMO page does not mention cremated remains or ashes, and no IMO or Protocol statement on ashes was found.
citation: London Convention 1972; London Protocol 1996 (IMO overview page)
quote: Under the Protocol all dumping is prohibited, except for possibly acceptable wastes on the so-called "reverse list".
notes: IMO page opened directly 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quote checked. The page gives 87 Parties to the Convention and 55 (elsewhere on the same page 56) to the Protocol: an internal inconsistency on IMO's own page. The treaty texts and Annex 1 'reverse list' were not opened; whether ashes fall under any reverse-list item (e.g. organic material of natural origin) is not stated by IMO and must not be asserted. Canada's CEPA Schedule 5 (CA-01) mirrors such a list and does not name ashes.

topic: MARPOL Annex V: what counts as garbage
rule: IMO describes Annex V garbage as food, domestic and operational waste, plastics, cargo residues, incinerator ashes, cooking oil, fishing gear and animal carcasses 'generated during the normal operation of the ship'. Annex V applies to all ships. Special areas with stricter rules: Mediterranean, Baltic, Black Sea, Red Sea, Gulfs, North Sea, Wider Caribbean Region and the Antarctic area. IMO does not mention cremated human remains.
quote: Under MARPOL Annex V, garbage includes all kinds of food, domestic and operational waste, all plastics, cargo residues, incinerator ashes, cooking oil, fishing gear, and animal carcasses generated during the normal operation of the ship
notes: IMO page opened directly 2026-11-21; quote checked. 'Incinerator ashes' means ship incinerator residue, not cremated human remains. Cremated remains brought aboard by a passenger are arguably not waste 'generated during the normal operation of the ship', but that is a reading, not an IMO statement. Do not say MARPOL allows or forbids scattering ashes. Annex V regulation text itself not opened.

topic: Burial at sea and scattering ashes
rule: A Marine Management Organisation licence is needed for a burial at sea (of a body) in English waters or Northern Irish offshore waters; GOV.UK states no licence or permission is needed to scatter ashes at sea after a cremation. For Welsh waters the page refers readers to Natural Resources Wales, for inshore Northern Irish waters to DAERA, and for Scottish waters to the Burial, Cremation and Death Certification Team.
citation: Marine and Coastal Access Act 2009; GOV.UK 'How to get a licence for a burial at sea in England' (updated 25 March 2026)
quote: You don’t need a licence or permission to scatter ashes at sea after a cremation.
appliesTo: England and Northern Irish offshore waters
notes: Opened directly 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200; https://www.gov.uk/burial-at-sea redirects here); quote checked. The ashes sentence sits in the section on English/NI offshore licensing, so it should not be read as a statement for Wales or Scotland (see UK-WAL-01, UK-SCT-01). Correction to round 1: GOV.UK names the Burial, Cremation and Death Certification Team (not the Marine Directorate) as the Scottish contact.

rule: The Environment Protection (Sea Dumping) Act 1981 (compilation in force 1 July 2026) does not mention human remains, cremation or ashes. Official guidance (DCCEEW / National EPA burial-at-sea page and sea burial permit form) reportedly states that scattering ashes at sea does not constitute burial at sea and needs no permit under the Act, while a body burial needs a permit.
citation: Environment Protection (Sea Dumping) Act 1981; DCCEEW sea burial guidance (not opened)
appliesTo: Australian waters; Australian vessels and aircraft
notes: Act text opened on legislation.gov.au 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200): grep found no human remains/ash wording. dcceew.gov.au and nationalepa.gov.au failed to connect from this environment; the 'no permit for ashes' statement is known only from search snippets of those official pages, so no quote is given. State/territory and Great Barrier Reef rules are separate (AU-GBR-01).

topic: Burial at sea regulations and ashes
rule: Not confirmed from an official page. The EEZ and Continental Shelf (Environmental Effects - Burial at Sea) Regulations 2015 reportedly apply to human remains other than ashes; EPA handles burials beyond 12 nm and regional councils within 12 nm (search summaries).
citation: Exclusive Economic Zone and Continental Shelf (Environmental Effects - Burial at Sea) Regulations 2015 (LI 2015/229)
notes: legislation.govt.nz returned HTTP 202 with an empty body (bot challenge; not bypassed) and maritimenz.govt.nz returned 403 on 2026-11-21. Whether the regulations exclude ashes, and any regional coastal plan rules, remain to be read.

rule: CEPA 1999 s.125(1): no person or ship may dispose of a substance in Canadian sea areas unless it is 'waste or other matter' (Schedule 5) and done under a Canadian permit. Schedule 5 lists dredged material, fish waste, ships/structures, inert geological matter, uncontaminated organic matter of natural origin and certain bulky substances; it does not mention human remains or ashes. The definition of 'disposal' excludes placement for a purpose other than mere disposal if not contrary to the Act and the Convention. Neither the Act nor any ECCC page read says whether scattering ashes needs a permit.
citation: Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999, ss. 122, 125, Schedule 5
quote: 125 (1) No person or ship shall dispose of a substance in an area of the sea referred to in any of paragraphs 122(2)(a) to (e) unless (a) the substance is waste or other matter; and (b) the disposal is done in accordance with a Canadian permit.
notes: Act opened directly on laws.justice.gc.ca 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quote checked (line breaks joined). canada.ca (ECCC disposal-at-sea pages) failed with a connection error from this environment and archive.org was unreachable. A search snippet of a BC government page says burial at sea falls under the federal Disposal at Sea provisions; that concerns burial generally and does not settle ashes. Whether ash scattering is 'disposal' or excluded 'placement' is an open question for ECCC's Disposal at Sea Program.

rule: Scattering ashes requires permission from the County Governor (statsforvalteren). On application from a person aged 15 or over, the statsforvalteren may permit the person responsible for their funeral to scatter the ashes 'for the wind'; permission may also be given after death where it is shown the deceased wanted scattering, and for a child's ashes when the next of kin wish it. Conditions may be attached.
citation: Gravplassloven (Lov om gravplasser, kremasjon og gravferd, LOV-1996-06-07-32) § 20
quote: Statsforvalteren kan etter søknad fra person som har fylt 15 år, gi tillatelse til at den som skal sørge for vedkommendes gravferd sprer asken for vinden.
appliesTo: Scattering on Norwegian territory and waters
notes: Opened directly on Lovdata 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200; consolidated text, last amended LOV-2023-06-16-40 from 01.07.2024); quote checked. Translation: 'The County Governor may, on application from a person who has reached 15 years, give permission for the person who is to arrange their funeral to scatter the ashes to the wind.' The statute does not distinguish land and sea; the statsforvalteren's practice on fjords or offshore areas is not stated here. Forskrift 1997-01-10-16 § on the cremation register notes such permission is recorded.

rule: German states treat a sea burial as the burial of an urn, not loose scattering. Baden-Wuerttemberg's official service description: a sea burial is the burial of an urn on the high seas outside the three-mile zone, lowered from a ship; the urn must be water-soluble, biodegradable and contain no metal; the municipality of the cremation place issues the exception permit for burial of the urn at sea, and the municipality of the burial ship's home port gives permission to commit the urn to the sea. Rhineland-Palatinate's 2025 law defines sea burial as burial of an urn on the high seas or in coastal waters under the coastal states' own rules.
citation: Baden-Wuerttemberg service portal (service-bw), 'Seebestattung'; Bestattungsgesetz Rheinland-Pfalz (in force 27.09.2025) § 11(7)
quote: Seebestattung ist die Beisetzung einer Urne auf Hoher See außerhalb der Dreimeilenzone. Dabei wird die Urne mit der Asche von einem Schiff aus im Küstengewässer beigesetzt.
appliesTo: Sea burials arranged from Germany; German coastal waters
notes: Karlsruhe and Heidelberg pages (both service-bw text) and the RLP statute PDF (mwg.rlp.de) opened directly 2026-11-21; quotes checked. Translation: 'A sea burial is the burial of an urn on the high seas outside the three-mile zone. The urn with the ashes is lowered from a ship in coastal waters.' The two sentences conflict (high seas vs coastal waters) on the official page itself. The coastal states' laws (Schleswig-Holstein, Hamburg, Lower Saxony, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Bremen) were not opened; a Schleswig-Holstein Landtag paper mentions water-law permits under WHG for urns in coastal waters. Loose scattering at sea from a German-arranged ceremony was not confirmed as lawful.

topic: Dispersal of ashes at sea and in nature
rule: CGCT art. L2223-18-2 limits where ashes may go; one option is dispersal 'en pleine nature'. Under art. L2223-18-3 the person responsible for the funeral must declare a dispersal in nature to the town hall of the deceased's birthplace, which records identity, date and place in a register. The Ministry of Justice's public guide adds that dispersal of ashes or immersion of a biodegradable urn is authorized 'en pleine mer'; dispersal on watercourses may be prohibited locally; a person using their own boat must respect distances from the shore and can ask the prefecture.
citation: Code général des collectivités territoriales arts. L2223-18-2, L2223-18-3 (as stated in the Government's answer to QE 17354, JO 1 September 2026); justice.fr 'Crémation'
quote: La dispersion des cendres ou l'immersion de l'urne (en matière biodégradable) est autorisée en pleine mer.
appliesTo: French waters; families of persons born in France (declaration)
notes: justice.fr (Ministère de la Justice) and the Assemblée nationale written answer (https://questions.assemblee-nationale.fr/dyn/17/questions/QANR5L17QE17354, published 1 September 2026) opened directly 2026-11-21; quotes checked. Translation: 'Dispersal of the ashes or immersion of the urn (in biodegradable material) is authorized at sea.' The Government answer: 'En cas de dispersion des cendres en pleine nature, une déclaration doit être faite à la mairie de la commune du lieu de naissance du défunt'. Legifrance itself returned 403 (bot protection, not bypassed), so the article text was not read directly; service-public.fr pages tried returned 404. No minimum distance figure is published on these pages.

topic: Dispersal of ashes at sea, lakes and rivers
rule: Law 130/2001: dispersal is allowed only in respect of the deceased's wishes, in designated cemetery areas, in nature or in private areas; it is prohibited in built-up areas; dispersal 'in the sea, lakes and rivers is allowed in stretches free of boats and structures'. Dispersal must be authorized by the civil-status officer on the basis of the deceased's express wish; unauthorized dispersal is a criminal offence (2 months to 1 year and a fine). It is carried out by the spouse or another entitled family member, the executor, a cremation association representative, or authorized municipal staff.
quote: la dispersione in mare, nei laghi e nei fiumi è consentita nei tratti liberi da natanti e da manufatti
appliesTo: Italian territorial waters and inland waters
notes: Text opened directly on parlamento.it 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200; Normattiva rendered only partially); quote checked. Translation: 'dispersal at sea, in lakes and in rivers is permitted in stretches free of vessels and structures'. Note: art. 3 sets principles for regional regulations, and penalty amounts are in lire (original text); regional laws add detail (see IT-02). Whether dispersal from a large cruise ship counts as a stretch 'free of vessels' is not addressed.

topic: Placing urns or ashes at sea (economic activity)
rule: Royal Decree 218/2022 amended RD 79/2019 so that the 'economic activity of placing funeral urns or funeral ashes at sea' needs a responsible declaration (declaración responsable) filed with the relevant Capitanía Marítima, replacing a case-by-case marine-strategy compatibility report. The declarant commits to: avoid protected habitats and species; certify urns are biodegradable; throw nothing else overboard except natural flower petals (never bouquets, stems or wreaths); keep a register of each service with date and coordinates; and comply with environmental rules. The form asks for the geographic coordinates of the zones used.
citation: Real Decreto 218/2022, de 29 de marzo (amending RD 79/2019, Annex III(d) and Annex IV)
quote: d) La presentación ante la Capitanía Marítima correspondiente de la declaración responsable del anexo IV, completada y firmada, para la actividad económica de colocación de urnas funerarias o cenizas funerarias en el mar.
appliesTo: Commercial operators placing urns/ashes in Spanish waters
notes: BOE text opened directly 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quotes checked. Translation: 'Filing with the relevant Maritime Captaincy of the completed and signed responsible declaration in Annex IV for the economic activity of placing funeral urns or ashes at sea.' Scope is the 'economic activity' (service providers); rules for a private family or a passenger on a foreign cruise ship are not stated. Regional mortuary-health rules and any distance limits were not found. A press claim of fines up to EUR 60,000 was not verified.

rule: No official Greek text was opened. A secondary summary attributes to Law 4483/2017 art. 133 a rule that ashes may be released at sea at least 1.5 nautical miles from the coast in a water-soluble container without pollutants. The official mitos.gov.gr page read covers only transfer of ashes from abroad (sealed urn and cremation certificate).
notes: mitos.gov.gr opened 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200): no sea rule. A targeted search for the official text of 4483/2017 art. 133 found nothing on et.gr or the Parliament site. The 1.5 nm figure is a lead only; check the FEK text (et.gr) before publication.

rule: No official Mexican rule on scattering ashes at sea was found. The Ley de Vertimientos en las Zonas Marinas Mexicanas (text opened) does not mention ashes or human remains. Press reports say the Secretaría de Marina (SEMAR) grants permits for depositing ashes at sea; not verified.
citation: Ley de Vertimientos en las Zonas Marinas Mexicanas (DOF 13-04-2020 version on gob.mx)
notes: gob.mx PDF opened 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); grep for ceniza/cadáver/restos humanos found nothing. SEMAR permit claim comes from El Imparcial and Diario de México (secondary-news). Ask the local Capitanía de Puerto.

rule: No Bahamian rule was found. The only official item seen concerns leaving the Bahamas with ashes (certificate of cremation), per GOV.UK guidance (search snippet).
notes: One search; no Bahamas government page on ashes at sea. Not opened directly. The Bahamas is a major flag state, so its law may govern scattering on the high seas from Bahamas-flagged ships.

rule: The British Virgin Islands government reportedly requires an application to the Ministry, with a permission-to-bury form and death and/or cremation certificates, for burials at sea of a body or cremated remains. Not confirmed: the page returned 404. No other Caribbean state was checked.
citation: BVI Government service 'Burials at sea (body or cremated remains)'
notes: URL from search returned HTTP 404 on 2026-11-21; content known only from a search summary. MARPOL treats the Wider Caribbean as a special area for garbage (INT-05), which does not by itself address ashes.

topic: MHLW guideline for scattering businesses (散骨)
rule: The MHLW guideline (from a FY2020 research project) defines scattering as grinding lawfully cremated bones to powder and scattering them on land or water. Scattering businesses must comply with laws including the Burial Act, Penal Code, Waste Management Act and Marine Transportation Act and local ordinances; at sea, scatter in waters at least a certain distance from the coast (set for local conditions); on land only in pre-identified areas excluding rivers and lakes; grind bones so their shape is not visible; respect residents, landowners and fishers; do not drop plastic or vinyl grave goods.
citation: 厚生労働省「散骨に関するガイドライン（散骨事業者向け）」(令和2年度厚生労働科学特別研究事業)
quote: 海洋の場合 海岸から一定の距離以上離れた海域（地理条件、利用状況等の実情を踏まえ適切な距離を設定する。）
notes: PDF opened directly 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200), linked from MHLW page https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/seisakunitsuite/bunya/0000123872.html; quote checked. Translation: 'At sea: in sea areas a certain distance or more from the coast (an appropriate distance is to be set in light of geography, usage and other actual conditions).' No numeric distance is given. Note the guideline excludes rivers and lakes for land scattering ('河川及び湖沼を除く'). It is guidance for businesses, not a statute; municipal ordinances (e.g. some that restrict scattering) were not checked. The old URL 000704619.pdf returns 404.

topic: Sea scattering at a designated site
rule: NEA: next-of-kin may scatter cremated ashes at a designated site at sea. The Maritime and Port Authority has designated a site 3.2 km east of Raffles Lighthouse, usable daily 7am to 7pm; contact MPA's Port Marine Safety Control Centre (6325 2488). NEA plans a two-year pilot ferry service from the second half of 2027 (S$50 per application).
citation: NEA 'Burial, Cremation and Ash Storage' page
quote: The Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) has designated a site located 3.2 km east of Raffles Lighthouse, where sea scattering can be conducted. This can be done daily, from 7am to 7pm.
notes: Opened directly 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quote checked. Older material citing a site south of Pulau Semakau is outdated per this page. Whether scattering elsewhere in Singapore waters is prohibited is not stated in the quote; the page presents the designated site as the sea-scattering option.

rule: Marine protected areas carry their own rules, often stricter than general ocean-disposal law. US examples confirmed above (sanctuaries restrict discharges, including from cruise ships; NPS waters need a permit for ashes). Outside the US, protected-area rules were not checked.
notes: US part confirmed via eCFR; non-US part unverified.

rule: A cruise line's permission is a private policy, not legal authorization. The applicable law depends on where the ship is (port state or coastal state within 12 nm; flag state on the high seas), where the remains were loaded (MPRSA covers remains transported from the US) and whether the spot is a protected area.
appliesTo: Families planning a scattering on a cruise
notes: Analysis built from the confirmed US texts and the unverified international framework above.

topic: Remains loaded abroad, placed in US waters
rule: EPA: the general permit is not available for human remains transported from outside the United States for placement in US ocean waters within 12 nautical miles from shore; that needs an MPRSA special permit.
quote: The MPRSA general permit is not available for human remains transported from a location outside of the United States for placement in U.S. ocean waters within 12 nautical miles from shore.
appliesTo: Foreign-embarked remains on ships approaching the US coast
notes: Opened directly on 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quote checked word for word.

topic: Remains taken from the US into another country's waters
rule: EPA: it depends on the other country's laws; the MPRSA rules still apply to remains taken from the US, and the country whose waters are used must be contacted and its laws followed; some countries may prohibit burials at sea in their waters.
quote: Some countries may prohibit burials at sea in their waters.
appliesTo: Ships leaving US ports for foreign waters
notes: Opened directly on 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quote checked word for word.

rule: EPA: states may not authorize burials in ocean waters or relax the three-nautical-mile requirement, but may impose additional requirements within state jurisdiction.
citation: EPA, Burial at Sea FAQ (MPRSA sections 106(a) and 106(d))
quote: States may not relax the MPRSA General Permit requirement that burials in ocean waters must be conducted at least three nautical miles from shore.
notes: Opened directly on 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quote checked word for word.

topic: Scattering ashes at sea in Welsh waters
rule: No Natural Resources Wales statement on scattering ashes was found. GOV.UK sends burial-at-sea questions for Welsh inshore and offshore waters to NRW. The NRW page on activities exempt from a marine licence was read and does not mention ashes, cremated remains or burial.
citation: Marine and Coastal Access Act 2009 (Wales); NRW marine licence exemptions page
notes: NRW exemptions page opened directly 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); grep for ash/cremat/burial found nothing. A funeral-industry blog says no licence is needed in Wales; that is a lead only. Couldn't verify is not evidence that a licence is required. Ask NRW Marine Licensing.

rule: Scottish Government burial guidance states that an application for burial is not required for the scattering of ashes. The Scottish Government glossary says burial at sea (of a body) takes place from a boat in a pre-authorised location and is currently only permitted off the North West coast of Scotland, with the Burial, Cremation and Death Certification team as contact.
citation: Burial and Cremation (Scotland) Act 2016; Scottish Government 'Burial Regulations: guidance' (page 3); 'Funeral Payment and Funeral Poverty: glossary of terms'
quote: An application for burial is not required for the scattering of ashes.
appliesTo: Scotland (burial authority procedures); Scottish waters for burial at sea
notes: Both gov.scot pages opened directly 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quotes checked. The ashes sentence concerns the burial-application regime under the 2016 Act; it does not expressly address marine licensing for ashes at sea, so a sea-specific Marine Directorate statement is still open. Glossary quote: 'This is currently only permitted off the North West coast of Scotland.'

rule: The Department of Transport page says burial at sea is permitted by Irish law; voluntary guidelines recommend that cremation and scattering of the ashes at sea be considered rather than burial, and that any burial take place at least 50 miles from the nearest coast in at least 200 m of water. The page does not state whether scattering ashes needs a Dumping at Sea permit; the Dumping at Sea Act 1996 text read does not mention human remains or cremation.
citation: gov.ie 'Burial at sea' (Department of Transport); Dumping at Sea Act 1996 (revised)
quote: The guidelines recommend that cremation and the scattering of the ashes at sea be considered, rather than burial.
notes: gov.ie page opened directly 2026-11-21 (redirected from /en/service/de81b8-burial-at-sea); quote checked. Revised Act at revisedacts.lawreform.ie opened; no mention of human remains or cremation. The government recommends ash scattering but does not say expressly that no permit is needed; ask the EPA (Dumping at Sea) or the Department's Maritime Environment Division.

rule: The Governor of Svalbard (Sysselmesteren) may, on application, permit ash scattering on the archipelago. It may not take place in built-up areas or where it would otherwise be a nuisance, and conditions may be set. Permission requires that the deceased (over 15) applied, or that it is shown the deceased wanted scattering, or (under 15) the next of kin wish it. No memorial may additionally be erected at the scattering site or in a churchyard. Appeals go to the Ministry of Culture.
citation: Forskrift om kirkegårder i Longyearbyen og askespredning på Svalbard (FOR-2008-02-15-153) § 8
quote: Sysselmesteren på Svalbard kan etter søknad gi tillatelse til askespredning på øygruppen. Slik askespredning kan ikke finne sted i bebygde strøk eller dersom det for øvrig vil være til sjenanse.
notes: Opened directly on Lovdata 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200), § 8 as amended by FOR-2021-06-23-2222; quote checked. Translation: 'The Governor of Svalbard may on application give permission for ash scattering on the archipelago. Such scattering may not take place in built-up areas or where it would otherwise cause nuisance.' Updates round 1, which relied on a search snippet. 'På øygruppen' (on the archipelago): whether surrounding territorial waters are covered is not stated.

rule: Since 27 September 2025 Rhineland-Palatinate allows river burial: an urn of immediately water-soluble cellulose placed from a ship on the Rhine, Moselle, Lahn or Saar within the state, subject to water law. The deceased must have had their last main residence in Rhineland-Palatinate and have set out the burial form in a written instruction naming a person responsible.
quote: Die Flussbestattung ist die Beisetzung einer Ascheurne aus sofort wasserlöslicher Zellulose vom Schiff aus auf einem der oberirdischen Gewässer Rhein, Mosel, Lahn und Saar auf rheinland-pfälzischem Hoheitsgebiet, unter Beachtung der Vorschriften des Wasserrechts.
appliesTo: Rhine, Moselle, Lahn, Saar within Rhineland-Palatinate
notes: Ministry PDF opened directly 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quote checked. Translation: 'River burial is the burial of an ash urn of immediately water-soluble cellulose from a ship on one of the surface waters Rhine, Moselle, Lahn and Saar in Rhineland-Palatinate territory, observing water law.' This is urn placement, not loose scattering, and requires RLP residence: it does not authorize a river-cruise passenger from elsewhere. Other states (e.g. Bavaria) were not re-checked this round.

jurisdiction: Italy (Campania, Castellammare di Stabia maritime district)
topic: Coast Guard ordinance on dispersal at sea (example)
rule: Harbour Master ordinance: dispersal in the district's waters requires the civil-status officer's authorization (Law 130/2001; Campania regional law 20/2006). Dispersal is prohibited within 1,000 m of the coast, installations, port entry corridors, river mouths, mariculture buoys, the Punta Campanella marine protected area markers and any structure at sea; from 1 May to 31 October the minimum is 2 nautical miles. The Harbour Master must be notified at least 3 working days ahead with date, time, place and the authorization, and informed by phone or VHF 16 before going out.
citation: Capitaneria di porto di Castellammare di Stabia, Ordinanza n. 97 del 7 settembre 2023
quote: La dispersione è, comunque, vietata ad una distanza inferiore ai 1000 metri dalla costa
appliesTo: Waters of the Castellammare di Stabia maritime district only
notes: Official Guardia Costiera PDF opened directly 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quotes checked. Translation: 'Dispersal is in any case prohibited at a distance of less than 1,000 metres from the coast'. Seasonal rule: 'Nel periodo compreso tra il 1° Maggio e 31 Ottobre la dispersione è consentita ad una distanza non inferiore a 2 miglia dalla costa'. This is ONE district's ordinance (near Sorrento/Naples); each maritime district may have its own. Do not generalize the distances to all of Italy.

topic: Scattering ashes in state waters (sea and rivers)
rule: Rijkswaterstaat: relatives may scatter ashes in state waters (open water such as the sea or a river) without a permit, provided they keep sufficient distance from bathing-water sites and drinking-water intake points and do not hinder shipping.
quote: Het verstrooien van as in rijkswater (open water, zoals op zee of in een rivier) is toegestaan voor nabestaanden. U hoeft hiervoor geen vergunning aan te vragen, zolang u voldoende afstand houdt tot zwemwaterlocaties en drinkwaterinnamepunten.
appliesTo: Dutch state waters (North Sea territorial waters, major rivers)
notes: Opened directly 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quote checked (link markup removed). Translation: 'Scattering ashes in state waters (open water, such as at sea or in a river) is permitted for relatives. You do not need to apply for a permit, as long as you keep sufficient distance from bathing-water sites and drinking-water intake points.' Applies to 'rijkswateren'; regional/municipal waters may differ. No distance figure given.

rule: Decreto-Lei 411/98 art. 19: ashes from cremations other than those ordered by a cemetery administration may be placed in an ossuary/columbarium or grave, or handed in an appropriate container to the person who requested the cremation, 'their final destination being free'. Transport of ashes outside a cemetery is free if in an appropriate container (art. 6(4)). The decree contains no provision on scattering at sea or in rivers (including the Douro).
citation: Decreto-Lei n.º 411/98, de 30 de dezembro (consolidated, last amended Lei 14/2016), arts. 6(4), 19
quote: c) Entregues, dentro de recipiente apropriado, a quem tiver requerido a cremação, sendo livre o seu destino final.
appliesTo: Portugal, including coastal and river waters
notes: Consolidated text on the Procuradoria-Geral Distrital de Lisboa site opened 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quote checked (site encoding drops accents). Translation: 'handed over, in an appropriate container, to the person who requested the cremation, their final destination being free.' 'Free destination' is not an express authorization to scatter at sea or in the Douro; harbour-master (capitania) practice reported in the press (an internal Navy order since 1999) and municipal rules were not verified.

rule: The 2025 Cemeteries Act allows cremated remains to be scattered at a specially designated place inside and/or outside a cemetery, in accordance with a general act of the representative body of the local self-government unit where they are scattered. Sea scattering therefore depends on a local decision designating the place and conditions.
quote: Kremirane posmrtne ostatke tijela umrle osobe dopušteno je prosipati na posebno određenom mjestu unutar groblja i/ili izvan groblja, u skladu s općim aktom predstavničkog tijela jedinice lokalne samouprave na čijem se području prosipaju kremirani posmrtni ostaci umrle osobe.
notes: Official Gazette (Narodne novine) text opened directly 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quote checked. Translation: 'Cremated remains may be scattered at a specially designated place inside and/or outside a cemetery, in accordance with a general act of the representative body of the local self-government unit in whose area they are scattered.' The Act does not mention the sea expressly; which coastal municipalities have adopted such acts, and any harbour-master (lučka kapetanija) requirement, were not verified. Later amendment NN 80/25 mentioned in secondary sources not checked.

rule: Not verified from an official text this round. The Lower Austria Bestattungsgesetz 2007 on RIS (LGBl. 9480) reportedly requires a biodegradable urn or capsule for burial in a body of water, with the municipality where the water lies granting approval; loose scattering in nature reportedly not allowed.
citation: NÖ Bestattungsgesetz 2007 (LGBl. 9480), reportedly § 16(6) and the water-burial provision
appliesTo: Lower Austria (Danube stretch); other states differ
notes: RIS returned HTTP 503 on 2026-11-21 (two URLs tried). Content known only from a search summary and a vienna.at news article (round 1). Each Austrian state has its own law.

rule: Act XLIII of 1999 § 21(1): with cremation, ashes may be placed in an urn or scattered under conditions set by government decree. Gov. Decree 145/1999 § 34: ashes may be scattered at a designated cemetery place; outside a cemetery, on a property only with the prior consent of the owner (manager); scattering from aircraft needs an aviation authority permit. No provision specific to the Danube or other rivers was found.
quote: (4) A hamvakat temetőn kívüli ingatlanon a tulajdonos (kezelő) előzetes hozzájárulása után lehet szétszórni.
notes: Both texts opened on the official Nemzeti Jogszabálytár 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quotes checked. Translation: 'Ashes may be scattered on a property outside a cemetery after the prior consent of the owner (manager).' How this applies to a river (the 'manager' of the watercourse) is not stated: that is an open reading, not a rule. The June 2026 Dunabogdány news report (round 1) remains a lead.

rule: GOV.UK's Egypt bereavement pack (2026 version read) says cremation is allowed in Egypt but there are no official facilities; one unofficial crematorium in Alexandria can be used only with local-authority permission. Nothing on scattering ashes in the Nile was found.
quote: Cremation is allowed in Egypt but there are no official facilities.
notes: Opened directly 2026-11-21; quote checked. CONFLICT with round 1 (law-inland-waterways.json), which recorded GOV.UK as saying cremation is not available or permitted: the current page says it is allowed. Law 48 of 1982 (Nile protection) was not opened; no Egyptian government source on ashes in the Nile was found.

rule: No official Vietnamese or Cambodian source on scattering ashes in rivers or the sea was found. Vietnam's Decree 23/2016/ND-CP governs cemeteries and crematoria; a search did not surface any provision on scattering.
notes: Ministry of Construction consolidated PDF (moc.gov.vn) failed to load on 2026-11-21. No Cambodian source tried. Couldn't verify is not evidence of a prohibition or a permission.

rule: No GBRMPA rule on scattering ashes was found. GBRMPA's 2007 'Memorials management' guideline concerns physical memorials (written permission needed under the Zoning Plan 2003) and does not mention ashes.
citation: GBRMPA 'Memorials management within the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park' (2007); Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Zoning Plan 2003
notes: PDF opened 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200, 2 pages); no mention of ashes or cremation. Zoning Plan not opened. Ask GBRMPA whether scattering ashes needs permission.

rule: No Bermuda government rule on scattering ashes at sea was found.
notes: One combined Bahamas/Bermuda search returned nothing relevant. Bermuda is a common cruise flag state.

topic: Scattering cremated ashes in designated waters
rule: There are three Designated Areas in Hong Kong waters: east of Tap Mun, east of Tung Lung Chau, and south of West Lamma Channel. Applicants must submit form FEHB 198 to the FEHD and obtain approval before scattering, whether using FEHD's free ferry or their own vessel. Only the remains and limited flower petals may be thrown into the sea (CLIC).
citation: FEHD / Hong Kong Government Green Burial website; Application FEHB 198
quote: you have to submit the "Application for Scattering of Cremated Ashes in Hong Kong Waters" (FEHB 198) form to the FEHD and obtain its approval for the scattering.
notes: Government Green Burial page opened directly 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quote checked. Free ferry details and the petals-only rule are from CLIC (Community Legal Information Centre, HKU), https://clic.org.hk/en/topics/legal-support-for-tai-po-fire/After-death-arrangements/Sea-scattering (opened 2026-11-21): 'no objects apart from the remains and limited quantities of flower petals are allowed to be thrown into the sea.' The underlying regulation (Cap. 132BF) was not opened.

rule: Shanghai defines sea burial as scattering ashes into the city's designated sea area; residents using a sea-burial service organization receive a subsidy (4,600 yuan per set of ashes, of which 3,000 to the family). National rules naming sea areas were not found.
citation: 上海市民政局、上海市财政局《上海市节地生态安葬补贴实施办法》(沪民规〔2022〕12号)
quote: 海葬：指将骨灰撒散到指定海域的安葬方式。
appliesTo: Shanghai residents; Shanghai designated sea area
notes: Official Shanghai Civil Affairs Bureau PDF opened 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quote checked. Translation: 'Sea burial: a burial method of scattering ashes into a designated sea area.' Local rule only; Shenzhen has a similar definition (page failed to load). Not a national rule, and says nothing about cruise ships or foreigners.

topic: Madrid Protocol Annexes III and IV
rule: Annex IV (marine pollution) defines 'garbage' as victual, domestic and operational waste generated during the normal operation of the ship and prohibits disposal into the sea of plastics and of all other garbage (paper, glass, metal, incineration ash and similar), allowing only ground food waste at least 12 nm from land or ice shelves. Annex III requires waste to be reduced and certain wastes removed. Neither Annex mentions human remains or cremated ashes. IAATO's FAQ says all human activities in Antarctica need a permit via an Environmental Impact Assessment by a national competent authority.
citation: Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty, Annex III Art. 1-2, Annex IV Arts. 1, 5; IAATO FAQ
quote: "garbage" means all kinds of victual, domestic and operational waste excluding fresh fish and parts thereof, generated during the normal operation of the ship, except those substances which are covered by Articles 3 and 4
appliesTo: Antarctic Treaty area (south of 60 degrees S)
notes: Annex III (Att010_e.pdf) and Annex IV (Att011_e.pdf) opened directly on documents.ats.aq 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quotes checked. IAATO FAQ (https://iaato.org/faqs) opened: 'As for all human activities in Antarctica, a permit is needed.' No treaty text or IAATO page read expressly prohibits or permits scattering ashes; the CNN guide anecdote (round 1) is secondary. Whether a national authority would authorize it is unknown. Do not state that the Antarctic Treaty bans ashes.

jurisdiction: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
rule: GSGSSI permits scattering of ashes on South Georgia under conditions; not on the South Sandwich Islands. Only scattering (placed on the ground or cast into the air), no burial of ashes or containers; ashes free of other material, carried in a biodegradable container; written notification at least 60 days ahead with details of the deceased and the location; not where it may disturb protected wildlife; no plaque or memorial without a separate permit; the person must be entitled to enter under immigration rules. Notifications to the Chief Executive Officer (admin@gov.gs).
citation: GSGSSI Policy Paper 03-21 'Scattering ashes (human remains) and burial of human remains', in force 1 November 2021
quote: The scattering of ashes on South Georgia is permitted if it is carried out in accordance with the conditions outlined below. The scattering of ashes is not permitted on the South Sandwich Islands
notes: Official GSGSSI PDF opened directly 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200); quotes checked. The policy speaks of scattering 'on South Georgia' (ground or air); scattering in surrounding waters from a ship is not expressly addressed. Updates polar-protected-areas.json 'south-georgia', which had no rule.

jurisdiction: Ecuador (Galapagos National Park and Marine Reserve)
rule: No Galapagos National Park Directorate rule on scattering ashes was found.
appliesTo: Galapagos National Park and Marine Reserve
notes: One search returned only general visitor rules (guide required, no smoking) from secondary sites; none mention ashes. Ask the Dirección del Parque Nacional Galápagos.
